title: z5 again with the host tty raw/no-echo the moment it appears: is the shell drowned by the host's echo of the banner?
note: tried once 2026-11-18 (second round, plain background reader, research walleye-z5b-tried-raw-tty): raw -echo removes the '> ' and 'Permission denied' noise (0 of each in a 30 s capture) but the shell still returns no command output, only banner beats; next item: z6 = z5 with the banner stopped (or sent to /dev/kmsg only) once the shell is up, so the shell's answers are alone on ttyGS0
proof: z5 once from slot b with the HOST tty put in raw, no-echo mode the moment the node appears, before anything is read: `stty -F /dev/ttyACM0 raw -echo -hupcl` in a tight loop started before the boot (poll for the node every 0.1 s, run stty at once, once per appearance; note how many bytes had already arrived), THEN the banner capture for 30 s (cat), THEN tests/host/mainline-shell-read.sh (one fd, raw) once, after the banner shows 'shell alive'. Record: (a) did the '> ' prompts and 'ash: /: Permission denied' lines disappear with the host tty raw? (b) do the reader's commands now get answers (dmesg, uname)? (c) if not, the banner line's shell fields at the time. Expected if the hypothesis holds: the host tty has ECHO on by default, so every banner line the phone writes is echoed back into the phone's tty, the shell reads the banner text as commands ('> ' = an unfinished quote, 'ash: /: Permission denied' = a line parsed as running /), which also swallows the real commands. Then z4 and y2 were never silent for lack of a shell, only drowned: the reader must set the host tty raw/-echo BEFORE the first byte can arrive (stty in a loop on appearance), and the init should ignore input lines for a few seconds after start (or the shell start should wait for the first line from the host). Record the decision text for the reader in the record. Battery first; phone left in Android.

title: z6: replace the silent interactive ash by a plain read/exec command loop on ttyGS0 (the banner stays)
note: built: images-z6 (research walleye-z6-built); try queued as walleye-try-z6
proof: boot-z6.img = z5 (banner2 + shell state in the banner) with the console block REPLACED by a command loop that needs no interactive ash, no job control and no controlling terminal: after stty -F /dev/ttyGS0 raw -echo -hupcl, `while :; do IFS= read -r line < /dev/ttyGS0 || { sleep 0.2; continue; }; [ -n "$line" ] || continue; sh -c "$line" > /tmp/out 2>&1; cat /tmp/out > /dev/ttyGS0; printf '\n__END_%s__\n' "$n" > /dev/ttyGS0; done` (the end marker carries the command counter, which the reader matches) - read the existing reader's marker convention in tests/host/mainline-shell-read.sh and use exactly that marker, so the reader works unchanged; the banner keeps running (its lines are tagged WALLEYE-BANNER so the reader can ignore them) and also reports the loop's state (commands run, last command, last rc); banner lines never carry the end marker; check script, selftest with a fake phone running the same loop in a pty (the loop is tested on the host with a pty pair so the claim 'a line in gets an answer out' is measured); programmer review; hashes

note:
Way back with no hands: arm only when the type reads back as 0x01 (hard 0x07 only if warm restarted); the command loop never arms the watchdog on boot (a restart lands in a quiet loop); battery rule first. If the phone does not come back it waits for hands as before - so the read item and the warm choice come first. Expect after the bite: same slot, uptime reset, watchdog bootstatus CARDRESET.

title: The test a_fixture_runs_at_once_while_other_threads_spawn fails now and then with ExecutableFileBusy (ETXTBSY) and blocks landings: make it deterministic
note: Seen failing in the 'attended tries prove themselves' check on records-only PRs (885, 925) and on at least one other: each time a rerun passed. It costs a landing each time; small. Rank 3: behind the stage 2 work. | DONE (walleye-builder, 2026-11-24): cause read - the fixture wrote the script through a handle in the test process, so a sibling thread's fork inherited it and its exec of the script failed with ETXTBSY; the /proc wait before could not see a child between fork and its listing. Now a short-lived cat child writes the file and has exited before executable() returns, so the test process never holds a write handle. Measured on the lab: fixture test 200 runs and the whole suite 30 runs, 0 failures; the OLD code also passed 200 of 200 here, so the failure was not reproduced locally (it showed under CI load) and the fix rests on the cause, not on a seen failure. clippy and fmt clean; product code unchanged.
proof: tools/walleye-tries fixture::tests::a_fixture_runs_at_once_while_other_threads_spawn no longer fails with Os { code: 26, kind: ExecutableFileBusy }: the cause is read first (the classic race: a thread forks while another thread holds the freshly written executable open for writing, so the child inherits the write fd and exec fails with ETXTBSY): the fix closes the write fd before any thread can fork (write the file, sync, drop the handle, then spawn), or opens it with O_CLOEXEC and serialises the write with the spawn; the test runs 200 times in a loop in CI or locally without a failure (cargo test -- --test-threads and a shell loop), says so in the PR; nothing about the product code changes; clippy, fmt, review

note:
From walleye-pon-read-after-bite-the-way. Phone off by adb reboot -p (cable in, then out), author holds power+volume-down once, lab fastboot-boots the reader image and saves 0xC0..0xCB raw; states what outlives a key press and the bootloader.
go until 2026-11-28T02:25:47+01:00, outcomes: If pon-block passes its PON_PERPH_SUBTYPE check and 0xC0/0xC2/0xC5/0xC7 show the power-key (KPDPWR) power-on and no warm-reset reason, then PON registers survive the power-off, the key press and the bootloader, so the bite procedure can read a bite's reason in our image. If the subtype check passes but the reason registers read cleared (zero), then the bootloader or the key path clears them, so the bite read needs another reader (Android's getprop bootreason). If pon-block prints 'none' or the subtype check fails, then regmap debugfs does not show the PON block on this image, so the next reader is Android's getprop. Author's go 2026-11-28: 'ye go PON' (relayed by the Top Coordinator).
